title: Dizziness on standing after a new blood-pressure tablet

profile.context: Lives alone in a ground-floor flat, attends alone, daughter visits weekly; mild hearing loss in the left ear.

facts.text: Feels light-headed and dizzy when she stands up from a chair or gets out of bed.
The dizziness began about 10 days ago, roughly a week after starting a new blood-pressure tablet.
Worse on first getting up in the morning and when standing quickly; settles if she sits back down for a minute.
Feels like a swimmy, about-to-faint feeling rather than the room spinning.
Each episode lasts less than a minute and happens several times a day.
Rates it 6/10; nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop, but has not actually fallen.
No chest pain, palpitations, blackouts or weakness of the arms or legs.
Has had high blood pressure for about 15 years.
Started amlodipine 5 mg once daily about two and a half weeks ago, added by the practice nurse for high readings.
Takes bendroflumethiazide 2.5 mg (a water tablet) every morning for years.
Takes a small tablet for her stomach each morning; cannot remember its name (it is lansoprazole 15 mg).
Takes paracetamol 1 g up to three times a day for hip pain.
Has stopped going to her Tuesday lunch club because she is worried about feeling faint on the bus.
Worried the new tablet is causing it and wants to know whether she should stop it.

contradiction.first_says: Oh, it's been going on for months, I think.
